analysis:
Examined the changed lines in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml (env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release near line 112; validate-older-macos assertion build_sdk_version == '27.2' at head line 1444), plus the changelog and docs/developer/build.md updates. The workflow change tightens release policy. It sets the release-mode toolchain for the whole workflow and updates the signed-validation identity assertion to SDK 27.2. The signing and notarization steps (lines 578-998) are unchanged and still verify hardened runtime, entitlements, get-task-allow absence, the Developer ID designated requirement, a full CodeDirectory hash and a final-bytes SDK check against BUILD_SDK_VERSION. Registration, the 'already signed' guard and the publication path do not change. The registered binary hash and CDHash identity (A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054) are still computed from the final signed bytes. I found no weakening of attestation, the build-qualification inputs or secret handling.

Open integration questions are outside the supplied evidence. scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh is not shown, so the claimed behavior is unverified: release mode accepts only SDK 27.2 and Swift 6.4.2, DEVELOPER_DIR is exported consistently, and the qualification mode (which also accepts SDK 27.0) cannot reach release signing. The BUILD_SDK_VERSION and PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION plumbing and the resume-path 27.2 check are also not shown. The docs and changelog describe these controls but cannot prove them. A reviewer who sees the script should confirm that release mode fails closed. The doc changes make no direct security claims beyond that.
